# Oracles & Price Feeds 

Robinhood Chain uses [Chainlink](https://chain.link/) for onchain price data. Both crypto assets and Stock Tokens have Chainlink price feeds, so your contracts can read reliable prices directly onchain — including live prices for tokenized equities and ETFs.

## Reading a price feed 

Chainlink price feeds implement the standard `AggregatorV3Interface` . Read the latest price with `latestRoundData()` , accessed through the feed's proxy address:

```
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT pragma  solidity  ^0.8.

...

* Underlying share price: `feedPrice * 1e18 / uiMultiplier()`
* Share-equivalent units: `balance * uiMultiplier() / 1e18`

The economic value is identical in every case — only the presentation differs.

See Building with Stock Tokens for end-to-end examples.

## Available feeds 

Feed proxy addresses, decimals, and heartbeats are maintained by Chainlink. See the [Robinhood price feeds page](https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/price-feeds/addresses?network=robinhood) for the current list — it's the source of truth, so always read addresses and parameters from there rather than hardcoding them.

## Checking sequencer uptime (recommended on L2) 

Because Robinhood Chain is a Layer-2, verify the sequencer is up before trusting a price — during a sequencer outage, feeds can go stale. Chainlink provides an L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed for this; check it before reading any price:

```

Uniswap (v2, v3, v4, and UniswapX) is the primary DEX, which is why its routers and factory sit in the core table — nearly every swap you make routes through one of those contracts. If you want to understand what the routers actually do with your approvals and slippage settings, read our Robinhood Chain Uniswap mechanics guide. |

## How do I verify a Robinhood Chain contract address myself?

Do not trust this page blindly.

...

**Sanity-check the activity.** A real WETH or USDC contract has enormous transfer history and thousands of holders. A copycat deployed last Tuesday has a handful of transactions and a suspiciously concentrated holder list. If the activity profile does not match the contract's supposed importance, stop.
5. **Compare against a second independent source.** ChainList (chainlist.org/chain/4663) confirms network parameters, and aggregators like DefiLlama link to canonical token addresses. Two independent official sources agreeing is your green light. One Telegram message is not a source.

One more habit worth building: check the last four characters of any address before you confirm a transaction. Address-poisoning scams rely on lookalike addresses that match at the start. The tail is where fakes usually give themselves away.

## What about lookalike explorers and fake docs?

Verification only works if the sources themselves are real. Lookalike explorer sites — hoodexplorer.
org, robinhoodchain.wiki, robinscan — exist and are not official. A fake explorer can show you a fake "verified" contract, which defeats the entire cross-check. The official explorer is robinhoodchain.blockscout.com, the official docs are docs.robinhood.com/chain, and the official ChainList entry is chainlist.org/chain/4663. Our Robinhood Chain network details page keeps the full official-links list, including the RPC endpoint and chain ID, in one place.

## Which addresses do scammers fake most often?

Three patterns dominate, based on documented cases on Robinhood Chain since July 2026:

**Fake stablecoins and WETH.** A token named "USDG" or "WETH" with a different address, seeded into a Uniswap pool so it appears tradeable. You swap real ETH for a worthless clone. The defense is the table above: on Robinhood Chain there is exactly one real USDG address, one real USDC address, one real WETH address.

**Copycat memecoin tickers.

...

The verified WETH address is listed in the table above, cross-checked against docs.robinhood.com/chain/protocol-contracts and Blockscout, with its own last-verified date. Never take a WETH address from chat messages or search results — fake wrapped-ETH contracts are a documented scam vector on the chain.

### How do I know a token contract is real and not a copycat?

Match the full 42-character address against an official source, then check it on robinhoodchain.blockscout.com: verified source code, deep transfer history, and a broad holder base. Copycat tokens show recent deployment, thin activity, and concentrated holders. Ticker and logo prove nothing — only the address does.

### Is there an official explorer for Robinhood Chain?

Yes — robinhoodchain.blockscout.com, run on Blockscout. Sites like hoodexplorer.org, robinhoodchain.wiki, and robinscan are not official, and a lookalike explorer can display misleading contract data. Confirm network facts against chainlist.
org/chain/4663 and docs.robinhood.com/chain before trusting any explorer.

### Why did I get a worthless token instead of the one I wanted?

You almost certainly interacted with a copycat contract using the same ticker at a different address. This is the most common scam on Robinhood Chain. Verify the address against this directory before swapping, and read our honeypot checker and tokens-disappeared guides if it has already happened.

### Does Robinhood Chain use the same contract addresses as Ethereum or Arbitrum?

No. Robinhood Chain is a separate Arbitrum Orbit chain with chain ID 4663, and contracts deploy at their own addresses there. Never reuse an Ethereum or Arbitrum One address on Robinhood Chain without confirming it in the official protocol-contracts list — same-looking addresses on different chains are different contracts.

### How often are these addresses re-verified?

Every row carries its own last-verified date, and we re-check the full table against docs.robinhood.

## Is Robinhood Chain Safe?

Robinhood Chain benefits from meaningful structural protections. It settles to Ethereum, builds on Arbitrum's battle-tested Nitro stack, uses Chainlink for oracle data, and embeds [compliance monitoring](https://www.techtimes.

...

For traders, the practical takeaway is to understand exactly what a Stock Token legally represents, size DeFi yield positions conservatively, and treat the network as promising but unproven infrastructure. Tokenized equities are clearly here to stay, and Robinhood Chain is now the highest-profile test of how they scale.

## Frequently asked questions

How do you bridge ETH to Robinhood Chain?

Use the Arbitrum canonical bridge or approved cross-chain routes to move [ETH](https://www.datawallet.com/price/ethereum) and supported ERC-20s onto Robinhood Chain. Deposits usually confirm within 10 minutes; withdrawals back to Ethereum require a seven-day challenge period plus L1 gas.

Which wallets support Robinhood Chain?

Robinhood Wallet supports the network automatically, but any [EVM wallet](https://www.datawallet.com/crypto/best-ethereum-wallets) can connect manually using Chain ID 4663, ETH as the currency, the public RPC, and the Robinhood Chain Blockscout explorer.

### USDG is Now Available on Robinhood Chain as the Lending Asset in Robinhood's New Earn Product

**NEW YORK July 1, 2026**–** **[Global Dollar Network](../) (GDN) is excited to announce that Global Dollar (USDG) is now available on Robinhood Chain, an EVM layer 2 built on Arbitrum and purpose-built for tokenized real-world assets and onchain financial services.
This launch makes USDG the first stablecoin natively issued on Robinhood Chain, bringing a trusted, regulated stablecoin to one of the most anticipated new chains in onchain finance.

USDG also will become the default lending asset in Robinhood's new onchain, self-custodial Robinhood Earn product, where customers can utilize USDG and earn rewards through curated vaults. Deposited US dollars convert to USDG and flow into leading DeFi protocols to put those deposits to work and maximize returns from onchain activity. 

For users and developers on Robinhood Chain, USDG provides a reserve-backed dollar for settlement, liquidity, and onchain financial services, combining fast, low-cost, 24/7 transactions with reward-sharing for the network participants who drive adoption¹.

Issued by Paxos, USDG was built with distinct features to serve demanding onchain environments like Robinhood Chain:
- **Fully backed 1:1**: Global Dollar (USDG) is a single-currency stablecoin pegged to the US dollar.
USDG is fully redeemable from Paxos on a one-to-one basis for US dollars.
- **Native performance**: USDG is issued natively on Robinhood Chain while maintaining Ethereum compatibility for broader accessibility. USDG is also available on Solana, Ink, and X Layer.
- **Trusted and transparent**: Paxos publishes monthly reserve reports for all Paxos-issued stablecoins, including USDG, to ensure full transparency and reliability of financial data.
- **USDG powers Global Dollar Network**: GDN is the world's fastest-growing stablecoin network with unmatched economic upside.

This launch advances Global Dollar Network's vision of a regulated stablecoin built to power all enterprise use cases, including onchain finance. Robinhood Chain's speed and Ethereum-grade security, combined with Robinhood's broad reach and USDG’s transparent economics, create powerful new opportunities across tokenized assets, trading, and DeFi.
“USDG brings a trusted, fully reserve-backed dollar to Robinhood Chain, helping power the next generation of onchain financial services for our customers and developers. As we expand access to tokenized assets and self-custodial crypto products, regulated stablecoins like USDG will play an important role in making onchain finance more reliable, useful, and accessible.”

Gaëtan Thabot, Director of Partnerships at Robinhood Crypto

### About Global Dollar Network

Global Dollar Network is the world’s fastest growing stablecoin network with unmatched economic upside. Powered by Global Dollar (USDG), a US dollar-backed stablecoin issued by Paxos Digital Singapore and Paxos Issuance Europe, Global Dollar Network offers a transparent and equitable economic model that rewards partners for their contributions. Global Dollar Network partners include industry leaders such as Bullish, Kraken, Mastercard, OKX, Paxos, Robinhood, Worldpay and more.

### About USDG in the EU
Paxos issues USDG in the EU through Paxos Issuance Europe OY ("PIE"). USDG is fully redeemable from Paxos on a one-to-one basis for U.S. dollars. All USDG token holders in the EU have a right of redemption against PIE at any time and at par value for USDG. Further information is available at paxos.com/eu, and the EU USDG White Paper is available at www.paxos.com/terms-and-conditions/usdg-eu-whitepaper.

* **USDG** , issued by Paxos, is the first stablecoin natively minted on the network and remains backed 1:1 by dollars.

* Uniswap liquidity for USDG on Robinhood Chain hit **$8.5 million** within a single week of launch.

## Liquidity and Yield Opportunities on Robinhood Chain

USDG isn’t just sitting idle on the network. It’s already generating measurable trading liquidity and yield within weeks of the chain going live, a sign that early demand for the token is translating into real on-chain activity rather than speculative hype.

### USDG Liquidity Milestones on Uniswap

[Uniswap liquidity for USDG](https://en.cryptonomist.ch/2026/08/20/ethereum-buy-white-house-meeting/) on Robinhood Chain climbed to $8.5 million within just one week of the mainnet launch. For a brand-new token on a brand-new chain, that kind of fast liquidity buildup suggests traders were ready and waiting for a native dollar rail the moment it became available.

### What is Robinhood Chain and when did it launch?

Robinhood Chain is a Layer 2 blockchain built on Arbitrum technology, launched on July 1, 2026.

### What is USDG and how is it backed?

USDG is the first stablecoin natively issued on Robinhood Chain, backed 1:1 by US dollars via Paxos.

### How can users earn yield on USDG deposits on Robinhood Chain?

Users can earn about 7% APY on USDG deposits via Morpho vaults through Robinhood’s Earn product, which includes insurance provisions.

### What benefits does the Aster platform offer for USDG trading?

Aster supports USDG deposits and withdrawals on Robinhood Chain without requiring KYC, allowing decentralized perpetual futures and spot trading via self-custody wallets.
